records.title: GEMINI: Fast Failure Recovery in Distributed Training with In-Memory Checkpoints
records.reason: GEMINI is a distributed training system for checkpointing model states in host CPU memory and recovering training after failures. Its checkpoint placement and network-traffic scheduling improve recovery speed while preserving training throughput; the paper explicitly targets static synchronous training. It does not study inference-time execution or serving and is outside the inference-focused scope.

records.title: StoreLLM: Energy Efficient Large Language Model Inference with Permanently Pre-stored Attention Matrices
records.reason: StoreLLM stores attention/KVQ matrices so inference can use storage reads instead of recomputation. The paper reports 1.45x energy efficiency versus LazyLLM with a 5.05% delay increase; alternative configurations report 2.64x and 2.83x energy-efficiency gains. This is a direct LLM inference energy/latency system contribution.

records.title: Cache-Craft: Managing Chunk-Caches for Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation
records.reason: Cache-Craft manages reusable KV states for arbitrary retrieved text chunks in RAG, selectively recomputing to preserve output quality and managing storage/eviction to hide overhead. With production workloads and synthetic data it reports 51% less redundant computation than prefix caching and 75% less than full recomputation; with continuous batching it reports 1.6x throughput and 2x lower end-to-end response latency than prefix caching for Llama 3 8B and 70B. This directly optimizes RAG inference.

records.title: RefreshKV: Updating Small KV Cache During Long-form Generation
records.reason: RefreshKV alternates full-context attention with attention over a smaller, dynamically refreshed KV subset during long-form generation. Query-vector similarity triggers full attention, which refreshes the partial cache; partial steps reduce attention computation and KV movement. Tests on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2-7B report comparable decoding speed to eviction baselines while improving long-form quality. The method keeps the full KV cache in memory, so its contribution is decode-time compute/latency reduction rather than total KV-memory reduction. This is direct inference-time KV-cache work.

records.title: CAKE: Cascading and Adaptive KV Cache Eviction with Layer Preferences
records.reason: CAKE allocates KV cache budgets according to layer-specific spatial attention dispersion and temporal shifts, then cascades eviction during prefill to keep peak memory within budget; its new eviction indicator accounts for tokens whose importance changes during decoding. On LongBench and NeedleBench it reports maintaining performance with 3.2% of full KV cache and over 10× decoding-latency speedup over full cache at 128K context with FlashAttention-2. This is direct KV-cache inference optimization.
